question: An engineer upgrades the bash on the Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch.
context:
guestshell:~$ sudo [MISSING_COMMAND] /bootflash/bash-4.2_8642465284455a-r8x86_64.rpm.rpm
Preparing...
#################################### [100%]
1:bash ################################### [100%]
update-alternatives: Linking //bin/sh to /bin/bash
Which command must be used to complete the task?
theory: RPM packages on the Nexus Bash shell are managed with the standard rpm command-line tool: the '-U' flag upgrades (or installs) the package, '-h' prints hash-mark progress, and '-v' adds verbose output — exactly matching the 'Preparing... [100%]' progress bar shown in the exhibit. 'upgrade -U' and 'update -vh' aren't valid rpm invocations, and 'rpm -qa' only lists already-installed packages without installing anything new. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools)
